scope: Independent visible desktop pixel review of exactly seven existing captures: course readability, heading wrapping, separators, figure framing and labels, and incoherent clipping or overlap.

courseFacts.basis: Supplied bounded-review facts and existing desktop DOM evidence; no source or full-text re-review.

displayContract.fig-212: instructional mechanical analogy, scroll media fixed at 640px

observations.detail: The complete vertical course display maintains a consistent centered reading column, distinct paragraph spacing, and visible bold emphasis. All five faint horizontal separators remain clear of text. Figures and their course captions are separated from adjacent prose; the final paragraphs end with bottom whitespace. No incoherent clipping or overlap is visible.

This capture shows the page top, not a scrolled polarization-definition region. The serif heading wraps to two lines with the final word 'light' alone on line two. The wrap is uneven but readable, within the column, and clear of the printed-page line and opening prose. Body text has clear glyphs, comfortable line spacing, and no horizontal clipping. The bottom edge is an ordinary viewport boundary in a scrolling page, not a broken container.

The top title, input/output labels, and bottom rotation label are readable and fully inside the frame. The plate, beam arrows, curved rotation marks, and observer symbol have visible margins; no text collides with the drawing.

All three vertically stacked subfigures are fully visible in the supplied tall capture. Panel headings, plate numbers, axis face-view labels, and output labels remain distinct and readable. Spacing separates each panel from the next; labels and diagram outlines are not clipped or incoherently overlapped.
The centered drawing and full bottom label are framed with whitespace. Gray outlines and label text remain legible against white; the intentional central arrow intersection does not obscure a label.
The plane outline, plate, arrows, letter p, and bottom label fit within the image. The letter and label remain separate from strokes, with no cropped extremities or text overlap.

At the fixed 640px media width, the two-line top labels, endpoint labels, end-view heading, opening labels, and two bottom statements are readable and fully framed. The rope/box drawing and lower end views occupy distinct vertical bands. No label collision or horizontal clipping is visible on desktop.

domReport.reusedChecks: Existing actual-text-size, layout, font, paragraph, and error checks only; no DOM or browser rerun.

limitations: PASS applies only to these hash-bound isolated headless offline desktop pixels. It is not headed acceptance, production verification, mobile review, or complete-course approval.

The image tool automatically resized the full-course capture from 1440x9644 to 896x6000 for inspection. No crop, reopen, or replacement image was made. Whole-course observations therefore concern visible composition and apparent readability, not native-resolution inspection of every prose glyph.

The file named en-desktop-polarization-viewport.png shows the page top rather than the polarization-definition region. That later region is covered only by the downscaled full-course capture and reused DOM evidence; no additional close-up was obtained.
Chinese source-bound machine ARIA labels remain retained and disclosed. No complete English accessibility certification, screen-reader review, or keyboard-interaction certification is claimed.
Existing DOM platform-font evidence is reused, not independently rerun. This pixel review does not certify embedded fonts, embedded raster glyphs, font portability, or all declared font faces.
Figure 209 exceeds one viewport in height; its supplied full figure capture was reviewed, not scrolling interaction. Figure 212's scroll contract was reused; no scroll interaction was tested.
Prior science, bilingual, source, and figure-semantic approvals are reused as directed. No source pages, answer keys, lesson source, or full text were independently re-reviewed.
